title: ar or ir er ow oi ear air · ur aw ore ou oy
cando: read the vowel sounds that are neither short nor long

about.text: In this lesson you learn the sounds ar, or, ir, er, ow, oi, ear, air, ur, aw, ore, ou, oy, are. You hear each sound, you write its letters, and then you read words and a short text with them.
goals: Say the sound for each new spelling
Read a word that has one in it
Write a word that has one in it
Know where in a word each one goes
Read the new words out loud

chapters.title: ar or ir er, ow oi, ear air
chapters.text:
This is Lesson 10.
These sounds are not short and not long.
They are their own sounds.
Four of them use the letter r.
Listen. Ar. Car. c. ar. Two sounds.
Not c, a, r. Two sounds only.
Next. Or. Fork. f. or. k. Three sounds.
Next. Ir. Bird. b. ir. d. Three sounds.
Next. Er. Her. h. er. Two sounds.
Now listen to those last two again.
Bird. Her. Ir and er.
They are the SAME sound.
Two spellings. One sound. That happens a lot.
You learn which word takes which by reading.
Now two more.
Ow. Cow. c. ow. Two sounds.
It is the sound you make when it hurts.
Oi. Coin. c. oi. n. Three sounds.
One sound, not two. Not o then i.
Two more you will meet in the words.
Ear. Hear. h. ear. Two sounds.
Air. Hair. h. air. Two sounds.
Hear and hair. Listen. Hear. Hair.
They look close. They are not the same.
Hear is what your ears do.
Hair is what grows on your head.
You can read most short words in English.
Next come new ways to write sounds you know.
Well done.

chapters.title: ur aw ore, ou oy, are eer
chapters.text:
The last of the vowels.
First, three that you already have.
In the first part of this lesson you met ir and er.
Bird. Her. One sound, two spellings.
Here is the third. Ur. Turn. Burn.
Ir, ur and er. One sound. Three spellings.
Next. In the first part you met or. Fork.
Here are two more ways to write it.
Aw. Saw. Law. Draw.
Ore. More. Store. Before.
Or, aw and ore. One sound. Three spellings.
Now two pairs.
Ou. House. Out. About.
Listen. That is the cow sound from the first part.
Ow in cow. Ou in house. The same.
And oy. Boy. Toy. Joy.
That is oi from the first part. Coin. Boy.
Oi in the middle. Oy at the end.
That is a real rule and it holds.
Two more that turn up in the words.
Are, as in care. And eer, as in near.
Near uses ear, which you know from hear.
Now one odd word. Work.
It has or in it. But it does not say or.
Work. It says the er sound.
There is a reason, and it is useful.
After a w, the letters or say er.
Work. Word. World. Worse. Worm.
All of them. Every time.
You have all the vowels now.

sounds.about: Two letters, one sound: ar. The a joins an r and makes one sound.
Two letters, one sound: or. The o joins an r and makes one sound.
Two letters, one sound: ir. The i joins an r and makes one sound.
Two letters, one sound: er. The e joins an r and makes one sound.
Two letters, one sound: ow. It often comes at the end of a word.
Two letters, one sound: oi. It sits in the middle of a word.
Two letters, one sound: ur. The same sound as ir and er.
Two letters, one sound: aw. The same sound as or.
Two letters, one sound: ore. It comes at the end of a word.
Two letters, one sound: ou. It sounds like ow in cow.
Two letters, one sound: oy. It sounds like oi, and comes at the end.

reader.title: The Farm
reader.text:
I went to the farm in the car.
A cow was in the yard.
A bird sat on the cart.
I can hear the cow.
A girl fed the cow. Her hair was dark.
It is a hard job on a farm.

canDo: I can say the sounds ar, or, ir, er, ow, oi.
I can read words like car and fork.
I can write a word from its sounds.
I can read a short text out loud.
